steps: Start setting up your own company in month 4, about 3.5 months before you need it.
Use employer of record for your first hires until month 8, so you can hire straight away.
Move your team onto your own company in month 8.
flags: People who work only for you, full-time and under your direction, are usually treated as employees. Using contractors for them is risky, so employer of record is the safer first step.
Running a company where you do not speak the local language costs more, so the running cost has been raised by 30%.

review.summary: The recommended route is to set up the company's own local entity, starting in month 4, and to use an employer of record until the team moves across in month 8. Over 24 months this costs £97,500 against £127,300 for staying with an employer of record, a saving of £29,800.
review.driver: The financial check points to the own company, and the strategic check agrees, while the risk check is clear because no tax, regulatory or contract triggers were reported. The cost crossover happens at month 8, when headcount reaches 8, so the own company becomes cheaper as the team grows.
risks: Setup must be complete by month 8, which leaves only about 3.5 months after setup starts in month 4. Any delay would mean either paying employer of record fees for longer or hiring before the entity is ready.
The running cost has been raised by 30% to £3,250 because the company does not speak the local language. If that uplift proves too low, the saving shrinks.

The risk check is clear only on the answers given. Staff who work only for the company, full-time and under its direction are usually treated as employees, so contractors should not be used for them in the meantime.
